title: Onboarding Impact Sprint — 10/30/90 Playbook with Success Metrics
content:
Purpose
This is an operational playbook for the first 90 days of a new customer onboarding, structured as 3 short impact sprints (10-day kickoff sprint, 30-day adoption sprint, 90-day value realization). It’s designed for mid-market customers adopting Redwood’s inference platform (hosted API -> dedicated/private path). The goal: clear milestones, measurable signals for QBR + renewal readiness, and a compact set of playbook callouts for SEs and CSMs.

Audience
- Primary: CSM (owner), Solutions Engineer (SE), Customer Technical Lead
- Secondary: Product Ops, Account Executive, Support

How to use this doc
- Use the 10-day sprint to validate connectivity, quick wins (one integration), and baseline metrics.
- 30-day sprint focuses on adoption sonics (traffic, key routes, cost per inference).
- 90-day sprint proving ROI and preparing renewal/QBR asks.

Quick summary bullets (for handoff)
- Owner: CSM (named) — accountable for adoption milestones and renewal signals.
- SE owner: responsible for technical success (token usage, model pinning, latency targets).
- Success criteria to track: activation event (first 1k tokens / route), sustained daily active routes (>=3), error rate <1%, average p95 latency target met per route.

10-day impact sprint (Kickoff & Connect)
Objectives:
- Kickoff meeting (set expectations, roles)
- Basic integration validated: API keys, VPC/Private networking if used, test call that returns expected output
- Identify 1–2 “first-win” routes/features for immediate value (e.g., article summarization endpoint, support-triage reranker)
- Instrumentation baseline captured in Redwood Console

Checklist (10-day) — quick, copyable:
- [ ] Kickoff scheduled with stakeholders (CSM/SE/Tech lead)
- [ ] API key/environment access verified (hosted or dedicated)
- [ ] Sample calls executed and screenshots uploaded to shared doc 
- [ ] Define first-win route + success metric (ex: reduce manual triage time by 30% on sample set)
- [ ] Console snapshot taken (tokens/day, latency, error rate)

Notes + common blockers:
- Private deployments: coordinate with infra team for firewall rules; typical lead time 3–5 days.
- If customer uses on-prem, get network diagram asap; escalate to solutions-eng for VPN/handshake.

30-day adoption sprint (Increase usage & stabilize)
Objectives:
- Ramp to meaningful traffic on first-win routes (target: 10k tokens/day or customer-defined threshold)
- Tune batching/caching suggestions from Redwood Optimize; apply one configuration change and measure delta
- Validate model & quantization recommendations against golden prompts
- Establish scheduled weekly adoption check-ins (CSM + SE)

Measurement (30-day):
- Primary KPIs (track in CS dashboard): tokens/day, route DAU, p95 latency, error %, cost per 1k tokens
- Secondary KPIs: number of prompts failing quality threshold, number of rollbacks

Checklist (30-day):
- [ ] Weekly cadence running; notes stored in customer playbook doc
- [ ] Apply caching or batching change (A/B if possible) and log results
- [ ] Add 5–10 canonical prompts for quality monitoring; link to Eval run in Optimize
- [ ] Create a simple runbook for common errors (401, 429, 500)

Risks and mitigation (30-day):
- Sudden spike in traffic causing throttles -> enable burst capacity or route to fallback model variant
- Quality regression after quantization -> quick rollback plan and evaluation triggers

90-day value sprint (Prove ROI & QBR prep)
Objectives:
- Demonstrate business impact and operational stability to stakeholders
- Prepare QBR materials: topline metrics, cost delta vs baseline, quality comparison vs expectations
- Capture renewal signals and expansion opportunities

90-day deliverables:
- One page QBR snapshot: activation -> adoption -> impact story (before/after metrics)
- Renewal readiness checklist (usage thresholds met, support tickets <= threshold, SLOs met for 30 days)
- Recommendations for next phase (dedicated capacity, higher SLA, custom models)

Renewal signal examples (what to watch for):
- Positive signals: continued growth in active routes, executive stakeholder presence at QBR, >3 product teams using output, NPS/comments in feedback >8
- Risk signals: plateauing token usage for 30+ days, repeat quality complaints, multiple unresolved severity 2+ incidents

QBR template (short):
- Title: QBR — <Customer> — 90-day summary
- Executive summary (1 paragraph): adoption, impact, ask
- Metrics: tokens/day trend, cost per 1k tokens, latency p95, error rate, Top 3 routes by usage
- Wins: customer quote, productization of route, reduced manual effort estimate
- Risks & asks: items requiring exec signoff (budget, dedicated capacity, data access)

Instrumentation & data sources
- Redwood Console snapshots (link to Console route dashboards)
- Eval sets saved in Optimize for quality drift detection
- Support tickets from Zendesk/Jira (tag: <customer>-onboarding)

Templates (copy-paste)
- Kickoff email: "Hi <Customer Team>, thanks — scheduled kickoff on <date>. Please share API key role or IP allowlist. Our SE will run a quick smoke test and we’ll capture a baseline console snapshot."
- Weekly check-in agenda: 1) wins 2) issues 3) metrics 4) next actions

Operational playbook notes (practical tips)
- Prefer a short list of canonical prompts vs wide unstructured test set — easier to track quality drift.
- Use the Console token breakdown to find expensive routes; often a single malformed prompt causes cost spikes.
- If customer is cost-sensitive, prioritize batching & KV-cache for chat-like flows.

Open questions / follow-ups
- Should we offer a "10-day tech audit" as a billable add-on? pros/cons TBD with GTM.
- Internal: which SRE on-call to include when private deployments go live (assignments unclear).

Appendix: quick metrics baseline example (copy to customer playbook)
- Day 0 snapshot: tokens/day: 120, p95 latency: 420ms, error rate: 0.8%
- Target (Day 30): tokens/day: 10,000, p95 latency: <350ms, error rate: <0.5%
- Target (Day 90): route DAU >= 3, adoption across 2 product teams, documented ROI story

Notes to self (CSM shorthand)
- Slack: ping #cs-onboarding for infra holds
- Jira: create ticket with labels onboarding/<customer> and priority=high for network issues
- Quick wins: recommend dedupe at caller side for avoid duplicate tokens

This is intentionally concise — copy this into the customer-specific playbook and tailor the success metrics and thresholds to the use case (search, chat, summarization, reranking).
